sourceVsWasm.anonymousNote: 91 anonymous types declared vs 131 anonymous ids in the wasm; node-types.json deduplicates identical anonymous tokens that the id table lists once per id, so the anonymous counts are not expected to agree and are not part of the proof. The named and field sets agree exactly in both directions. The patches add no node type and no field, so this proof is unchanged in kind by adopting them — only the id count moves (188 -> 189).

corpus._note: Enumerated by RULE (filenames Makefile/makefile/GNUmakefile/Makefile.am/Makefile.in, or suffix .mk), not by a hardcoded list, and every file is sha256'd with its repository pinned, so a later run that draws a different set says so rather than quietly reporting different numbers. A census filtered by what the analyzer already handles cannot find what it drops, so nothing is filtered here. `completeness-inventory` prints 46 classified types against this spec's 44 entries, and the difference is NOT a gap: the wasm carries 46 named NODE IDS for 44 unique names, because `word` and `text` each occupy two ids (the grammar gives the bare and quoted forms separate ids). The 44 unique names are what src/node-types.json declares and what the two sets agree on exactly, in both directions.
corpus._errorNote: Three of the corpus's 99 files produce a parse error, and the three are NOT the same thing. boundary/Makefile (8 ERROR nodes) and vault/Makefile (1) are real grammar gaps — MAKE-G3 and MAKE-G4. torrentinim/Makefile reports hasError=true with ZERO ERROR and ZERO MISSING nodes: the grammar's error bit is set by a hidden recovery token web-tree-sitter does not surface, so the engine emits its generic warning (engine.ts:1264). That file parses into the CORRECT tree and the analyzer's output for it is correct, so it is not a file error. Counting it as one would have hidden the two real gaps behind a third phantom.

handled_verified._rule: The analyzer produces a SYMBOL, an EDGE, or a METADATA ANNOTATION on a symbol from this node type, AND the behaviour is pinned by a fixture in validation/m14/fixtures/make/ or measured over the corpus. A type is not in this bucket on the strength of the grammar declaring it or a `case` label existing -- a `case` for a node type the walk can never reach is a PHANTOM, which is precisely how the dead `endif_directive` branch and the `undefine_directive` branch both survived until the corpus was asked which declared types it never fires.

_perType.makefile: becomes the per-file module symbol; the source of every contains/exports/imports edge
_perType.variable_assignment: Constant symbol, trimmed name, operator from node positions, contains edge, references to $(VAR) in the value
_perType.shell_assignment: Constant symbol with the `!=` operator and the shell command as its value; pinned by make/directive-flags
_perType.define_directive: FUNCTION symbol, not a Constant — a `$(call NAME)` that resolves to a constant is a callee that cannot be called
_perType.rule: one Function symbol per non-special target, contains + exports edges, and dependency edges for every prerequisite group including order-only
_perType.targets: read for literal targets; a computed target (`$(UI_TARGETS):`) yields a reference instead of inventing a buildable symbol
_perType.prerequisites: every `|`-separated group, 172 order-only prerequisites in this corpus
_perType.word: the name/value text of assignments, references, targets and callees
_perType.text: the recorded value of an assignment
_perType.list: the path list of an include and the name list of a bare `export`
_perType.variable_reference: $(VAR) — a references edge when this file declares VAR, a uses edge otherwise
_perType.substitution_reference: $(VAR:.c=.o) — a SIBLING of variable_reference, not a child; reading only the latter lost all 9 in this corpus
_perType.automatic_variable: $@ $< $^ — a uses edge; it names nothing any file can declare, which is exactly what the uses class is for
_perType.function_call: $(call NAME) becomes a calls edge to the macro; builtin functions are not edges
_perType.arguments: the callee of a `$(call …)` is its first comma-separated field; the grammar gives the call node no child of its own for the name
_perType.include_directive: imports edge sourced at THIS file's module node, never a hardcoded name
_perType.shell_function: what `include $(shell …)` actually produces — checked by measurement, not by guessing the node type
_perType.shell_command: the body of a shell function; walked, declares nothing
_perType.export_directive: an exports edge; `export NAME` with no `=` wraps a `list` and is the only place that name appears
_perType.unexport_directive: retracts BOTH the exported flag and the `exports` edge; clearing only the flag left the graph contradicting the symbol table. Pinned by make/directive-flags.
_perType.override_directive: records `isOverride` on the variable it wraps. The flag is applied AFTER the walk, because the assignment nested inside the directive has not run yet when the directive is read -- applying it eagerly dropped the annotation in the one-line spelling people actually write. Pinned by make/directive-flags and measured at tree-sitter-lua/Makefile:25.
_perType.private_directive: records `isPrivate`, same deferral and same reason as override_directive. Pinned by make/directive-flags.
_perType.undefine_directive: records `isUndefine`. Its operand is a bare word in the `variable` FIELD with no named children, so this needed the field rather than a child search -- and until make/directive-flags existed the child search made the branch unreachable.
_perType.conditional: counted for complexity and walked; the declarations inside are attributed to their own owners
_perType.string: a quoted value; recorded as the value of its assignment
_perType.raw_text: a macro body; recorded as the macro's value and not scanned for references, because Make does not expand it in place

_verification.shell_assignment: fixture make/directive-flags (DYNAMIC on line 15); 0 corpus occurrences
_verification.unexport_directive: fixture make/directive-flags (EXPORTED, lines 7-8: the `exports` edge must be RETRACTED, not just the flag cleared); 0 corpus occurrences
_verification.override_directive: fixture make/directive-flags (OVERRIDDEN, line 12); MEASURED on the corpus at tree-sitter-lua/Makefile line 25, where CFLAGS now records isOverride
_verification.undefine_directive: fixture make/directive-flags (GONE, line 14); 0 corpus occurrences. This branch was a PHANTOM before the fixture: `undefine VAR` carries a bare word in its `variable` FIELD and has no named children, so the search for a nested variable_assignment could never match.

internal_silent._rule: A construct that correctly produces NO symbol and NO edge. These are walked rather than skipped, because a reference nested inside one of them is still a real reference -- the bug this bucket exists to prevent is `continue`-ing past a container and losing the declarations under it. Two reasons a type lands here, and which one applies is recorded per type: (a) it is a container, literal or escape whose contents are handled by their own types, or (b) the thing it names is something the file does not declare, so a symbol for it would assert a declaration that does not exist.

_perType.recipe: transparent: references inside are attributed to the enclosing target, not to the recipe
_perType.comment: a comment declares nothing; 663 in this corpus
_perType.escape: an escaped `$`; it is a character, not a name — 121 in this corpus
_perType.concatenation: a glued path such as `$(TEST_EBIN)/%.beam`; read as its parent's text rather than as a name of its own
_perType.pattern_list: only ever produced INSIDE an ERROR node, by the grammar's partial recovery on target-specific variables; carrying it as silent rather than handled is deliberate, because the analyzer cannot act on a node the grammar itself rejected
_perType.archive: declared by the grammar, 0 occurrences in this corpus, and names no declaration
_perType.paths: the operand list of a vpath; 0 occurrences, and its parent vpath_directive already records the fact
_perType.vpath_directive: reason (b): `vpath %.c src` names DIRECTORIES and a wildcard pattern that the file does not declare, so it produces no symbol and no edge by design -- inventing either would assert a declaration that does not exist. It is not silent, though: it is recorded as the `Make vpath` pattern, and BOTH directions are pinned by make/directive-flags (the pattern present, no symbol invented). Before that fixture it produced nothing at all and nothing asserted it, and an unasserted silence is indistinguishable from an unimplemented construct.

gap._description: Two findings, both recorded here rather than left for a reader to discover: two declared grammar features that are unmodelled and unexercised (MAKE-G1, MAKE-G2). The two GRAMMAR LIMITATIONS previously recorded here as MAKE-G3 and MAKE-G4 are FIXED — the residual in script/m12/make-corpus-errors.ts and make-corpus-measure.ts is now EMPTY, pinned to zero real ERROR/MISSING nodes. Those two pins went RED when the patched grammar dropped the residual from 2 files / 9 nodes to 0, which is the point of a pin: it failed on an improvement rather than being edited to match one.

gaps.description: `VPATH = src` is a declared node type the analyzer does not model, so the search path is not recorded. 0 occurrences across all 99 corpus files, so there is no evidence to design against and no regression to guard. The sibling `vpath_directive` (the functional form) IS recorded, so the two spellings of the same feature are deliberately asymmetric pending corpus evidence for the assignment form.

`.RECIPEPREFIX = >` changes what a recipe line looks like, so ignoring it means recipe lines using a non-default prefix are not recognized as recipes. 0 occurrences in this corpus (every one of the 99 files uses a tab), so the exposure is unmeasured rather than known to be zero — recorded as open precisely because "no corpus evidence" is not the same claim as "no risk".

CLOSED by patching the vendored grammar, after the trade below was MEASURED instead of assumed. The target-scoped form `target: export VAR = value` was not parsed by tree-sitter-make 1.1.1: the line became an ERROR node, so 9 variable names (BOUNDARY_INSTALL_BINARY, SKIP_PLUGIN_BUILD, UI_CLONE_DIR, UI_COMMITISH, UI_DEFAULT_BRANCH, UI_VERSION_FILE, GOOS, GOARCH, AWS_PROFILE) were never extracted and the analyzer published error-recovery artefacts instead — `uses install -> BOUNDARY_INSTALL_BINARY=1` and `uses docker-build-dev -> GOOS=$(DEV_DOCKER_GOOS)`, i.e. whole assignment text used as a name. Cause: `variable_assignment` accepts an optional leading `list ':'` so `target: VAR = value` parsed, but `export_directive` puts the `export` keyword BEFORE the assignment and nothing allowed it after the colon. P1 adds that branch.

The original ruling was to REFUSE this patch, to protect the source<->wasm identity proof (0 missing / 0 extra, both directions, re-checkable offline) for 10 lines in 2 files. That trade does not survive measurement: the patch adds NO node type and NO field — 44 named / 24 fields before and after, zero added, zero removed — so the proof loses nothing and is re-established for the patched source at 189 ids / 44 named / 131 anon / 24 fields, 0 missing and 0 extra. Product level: 1,772 -> 1,781 symbols and 5,870 -> 5,880 relationships, with all 19 lost facts being error-recovery garbage or a reference re-attributed to its correct owner. The analyzer needed NO change, which is the strongest evidence the patch is well-founded: the constructs it repairs were already modelled, just unreachable. The pristine build and the patch are retained under grammars/tree-sitter-make/ab/ so the A/B stays re-runnable.

gaps.description: CLOSED by patching the vendored grammar. `MAIN_PACKAGES=$$($(GO_CMD) list -tags enterprise ./... | grep -v vendor/)` in vault/Makefile line 5 is a shell command inside an escaped-dollar expansion with a nested reference; tree-sitter-make 1.1.1 routed `$$` into variable_reference / substitution_reference / automatic_variable / function_call, none of which can parse a shell command head (spaces, pipes). `$$` is Make's ESCAPED dollar — Make does not expand it and hands `$( ... )` to the shell — so this is a modelling error, not a missing feature. P2 adds a hidden `_shell_escape` keyed on `$$` ONLY, so `$(FOO)` is still a variable reference, with the variable_reference/_paren_text ambiguity DECLARED as a conflict and resolved by dynamic precedence: a static precedence would discard one reading for every input instead of only for the inputs where it is wrong. `MAIN_PACKAGES` is now declared. The `$(GO_CMD)` inside is correctly NOT a Make reference, because Make does not expand it.
gaps.fixedBy: grammar patch P2 (grammars/tree-sitter-make/grammar.js `_shell_escape`); measured in fixtures/make/out/grammar-ab.json

summary.note: G1/G2 remain OPEN and are corpus-COVERAGE gaps (0 occurrences in 99 files), not correctness defects: no corpus evidence is not the same claim as no risk.

design_decision._rule: A question the grammar raises that has no single right answer, adjudicated on measurement and recorded with the numbers that settled it.

decisions.question: The relationship taxonomy carries ten kinds. Can GNU Make express inheritance, implementation, override or construction?
decisions.resolution: NOT APPLICABLE, and each half is measured rather than asserted. `extends`/`implements`: Make has no type declaration, no base clause and no interface implementation among its 44 named node types, so the kinds are not merely unused but inexpressible. `instantiates`: Make has no `new` and no object construction; a recipe is a shell command, not an expression that yields a value. `overrides`: this is the one kind with a real construct — `override VAR = value`, 2 occurrences in the corpus — and it is deliberately NOT emitted, because what an `override` overrides is a command-line or environment binding, which is not a symbol in the graph, so the edge would dangle by construction. The construct is not lost: the variable is recorded with `isOverride` on its symbol. So 6 of the 10 kinds are emitted (contains, references, uses, exports, imports, calls) and 4 are ruled N/A.

decisions.question: GNU Make has exactly one declaration level, so what does `contains` mean here, and what is the source of an `exports` edge?
decisions.resolution: A makefile is given ONE module symbol, named for the file, and it owns `contains` for every declaration and `exports` for every buildable target. The alternative — no module node — was measured and it is why the lane advertised almost nothing: with `exports` hardcoded empty and `imports` sourced at a literal "makefile", every include edge in a project collapsed onto one node and the file's public surface was unanswerable. Make targets ARE the file's public surface (an including makefile invokes them by name), so publishing them as exports is the semantics rather than a convenience. The module node is a real entity, not an invented one: it is the file, it is the unit the indexer already stores, and the per-file corpus census shows exactly 99 of them for 99 files.

decisions.question: Should a reference to something this Makefile does not declare be published as a project-internal reference, or as a use?
decisions.resolution: A `uses` edge, and the split is the whole point of the change. A Make prerequisite is usually a FILE (231 unresolved edge ends), a variable is often set by the command line, the environment or another makefile (187), and GNU Make ships builtins no file declares (160). Publishing those as `references` asserts a declaration that does not exist — before the fix, 112 edge ends dangled for a different reason entirely (the declaration existed but was captured WITH its operator, as `CGO_ENABLED?`). `references` is now emitted only when THIS file declares the target (1,564 edges); everything else is `uses` (788), labelled `builtin`, `external`, `external_prerequisite`, `local_binding` or `shell_variable` so the class is visible rather than pooled. Every unresolved end in the corpus was classified into exactly one of those buckets and NONE fell into a true-dangler class: fixtures/make/out/dangle-adjudication.json.

decisions.question: Where may a reference be collected from?
decisions.resolution: From wherever it appears, driven by the walk itself, rather than from two hardcoded branches. The previous analyzer asked for references only beneath a `variable_assignment` and a `rule`, so a bare top-level expression contributed nothing — and `$(foreach t,… $(eval $(call mk,$(t))))`, the idiom nomad/GNUmakefile uses to reify its package targets, is exactly that: a `function_call` directly under `makefile`. The corpus has one such site and it produced zero edges before this change. Each frame of the walk now carries the OWNER its references belong to, which is also what makes a reference inside a conditional the grammar swallowed into another rule's recipe attribute to its own rule instead of the outer one.

decisions.question: How is an assignment's name recovered, given that the grammar's `word` node can include the operator?
decisions.resolution: By trimming a trailing operator run BY CHARACTER CODE, never by regex. This is not cosmetic: for `CGO_ENABLED?=1` the `word` node spans `CGO_ENABLED?`, while for `CC:=1` it spans `CC`, so the two spellings of the same syntax produced different symbol names. Measured over the corpus that was 55 symbols named `CGO_ENABLED?`/`BUILD_TAGS+` and 112 edge ends that dangled by construction, because every reference names the clean identifier. Keywords reaching the same capture path are rejected the same way, which is what stopped `export` appearing as the target of six edges in boundary/Makefile.
